content.title: About
content.content: Egg yolk is the yellow part of a chicken egg that contains almost all of the egg’s nutrients: fats, proteins, vitamins, and minerals. Raw yolk is commonly used in cooking for sauces, desserts, and as a nutrient‑dense ingredient.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The yolk holds nearly all of the egg’s vitamins B, as well as vitamins A, D, E, and K.
About 55 % of an egg’s calories are found in the yolk.
Yolk color varies with the hen’s diet; more carotenoids produce a deeper yellow.
Raw yolk is a key ingredient in classic sauces such as hollandaise, mayonnaise, and certain custards.
Yolks contain lecithin, a natural emulsifier that helps blend fats and water.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and D
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision and immunity, while vitamin D is essential for bone health and immune function.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Yolk proteins contain all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains lecithin
items.content: Lecithin aids liver function and promotes normal fat metabolism.

items.title: Mineral dense
items.content: Yolks provide iron, phosphorus, calcium, and zinc, supporting blood formation, bone strength, and immune health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Vitamin E and carotenoids in yolk protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Raw yolk can be contaminated with Salmonella bacteria, so people with weakened immunity, pregnant women, and young children should prefer cooked eggs.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: A single yolk contains about 186 mg of cholesterol, which may be a concern for cholesterol‑restricted diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to yolk, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw yolk can be whisked into sauces (hollandaise, mayonnaise), added to smoothies, used in desserts (mousses, custards), or incorporated into baked goods. When consuming raw, ensure eggs are fresh and sourced from reputable suppliers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep eggs refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. Use raw yolk within 2‑3 days after separating from the white. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
